articles.title: Oil Price Today (October 29): Crude oil dips to $113 as diplomatic talks outweigh infra attacks. Can oil fall further?
articles.description: Crude oil price : In light of recent diplomatic talks surrounding potential U.S. military engagements with Iran, oil prices have taken a dip. These crude prices remain sensitive to the fluctuating situation marked by ongoing regional conflicts and the threat of further military interventions. Despite Iran's openness to negotiations, escalating hostilities from the Houthi faction targeting Saudi Arabia add to the uncertainty.

articles.title: India Closely Monitoring Tehran Talks Involving Pakistan, Says Centre
articles.description: The statement comes amid reports of discussions in Tehran aimed at de-escalating regional tensions and securing a ceasefire between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthi group, with Iran reportedly facilitating negotiations.

articles.title: $1 Billion For Peace? Saudi Arabia's Reported Offer To Houthis In Iran-Brokered Deal
articles.description: Saudi Arabia has reportedly offered $1 billion to the Houthis through an Iran-brokered deal to secure a ceasefire and halt attacks on the kingdom, Israeli media reported. No payment has been confirmed., Middle East, Times Now

articles.title: Egypt’s parliament approves military support for Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
articles.description: Egypt has approved military help for Saudi Arabia if requested as Houthi attacks threaten the kingdom and Red Sea shipping. The vote comes as Saudi officials hold talks in Iran amid regional efforts to prevent a further escalation of the fighting.

articles.title: Oil falls $2 as Middle East talks help ease supply worries
articles.description: Brent crude futures fell 1.8% to $113.72 a barrel on Tuesday as traders monitored Iran peace talks and renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia offered Houthis $1 billion for ceasefire, Iran to mediate: Report
articles.description: Saudi Arabia has reportedly offered Yemen’s Houthi rebels $1 billion in exchange for a ceasefire and an end to attacks on its infrastructure, according to Israel Hayom. Riyadh confirmed Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman’s visit to Tehran but did not confirm the alleged offer or a final agreement.
